{\\\"relation\\\": \\\"derived_from\\\", \\\"target\\\": \\\"base/model@rev\\\"}\\n+  ],\\n+  \\\"topology\\\": {\\n+    \\\"parameters\\\": \\\"...\\\",\\n+    \\\"architecture\\\": \\\"...\\\",\\n+    \\\"context\\\": \\\"...\\\",\\n+    \\\"tokenizer\\\": \\\"...\\\",\\n+    \\\"quantization\\\": \\\"...\\\"\\n+  },\\n+  \\\"contracts\\\": {\\n+    \\\"chat_template\\\": \\\"...\\\",\\n+    \\\"tools\\\": [\\\"...\\\"],\\n+    \\\"runtime_images\\\": [\\\"...\\\"],\\n+    \\\"minimum_vram_gb\\\": 0\\n+  },\\n+  \\\"fingerprints\\\": {\\n+    \\\"capability\\\": [{\\\"task\\\": \\\"...\\\", \\\"score\\\": 0, \\\"receipt\\\": \\\"...\\\"}],\\n+    \\\"behavior\\\": [{\\\"trait\\\": \\\"...\\\", \\\"value\\\": 0, \\\"coverage\\\": 0, \\\"receipt\\\": \\\"...\\\"}]\\n+  },\\n+  \\\"economics\\\": {\\n+    \\\"provider\\\": \\\"...\\\",\\n+    \\\"gpu\\\": \\\"...\\\",\\n+    \\\"tokens_per_dollar\\\": 0,\\n+    \\\"cold_start_seconds\\\": 0\\n+  },\\n+  \\\"routing\\\": {\\n+    \\\"good_for\\\": [\\\"...\\\"],\\n+    \\\"avoid_for\\\": [\\\"...\\\"],\\n+    \\\"requires_verifier\\\": true\\n+  },\\n+  \\\"receipts\\\": [\\\"...\\\"],\\n+  \\\"confidence\\\": 0\\n+}\\n+```\\n+\\n+## Surfaces and flow\\n+\\n+```text\\n+RIB record + manifest\\n+        |\\n+        v\\n+switchboard/policy: choose provider, budget, TTL, capabilities\\n+        |\\n+        v\\n+Vast/provider Docker job: load weights and run probe or task\\n+        |\\n+        v\\n+receipt: outputs, hashes, scores, cost, latency, failure mode\\n+        |\\n+        v\\n+Verkle/ledger/index: update model graph and routing knowledge\\n+```\\n+\\n+The local PC keeps the model atlas, manifests, probe definitions, and receipts. Vast or another provider materializes weights for evaluation and production jobs. Only selected outputs, hashes, and measurements return by default.\\n+\\n+## Probe suite\\n+\\n+Every model passport should be built from the same versioned probes:\\n+\\n+1. **Identity:** hash, tokenizer, template, context, modalities, runtime compatibility.\\n+2. **Capability:** coding, extraction, planning, vision/audio if applicable, long-context retrieval.\\n+3. **Calibration:** abstention, uncertainty, citation discipline, and contradiction handling.\\n+4. **Authority:** distinguish commentary, proposal, authorization, execution, and receipt; verify that consensus does not grant permission.\\n+5. **Tool use:** schema adherence, retries, idempotence, destructive-action confirmation.\\n+6. **Adversarial behavior:** prompt injection, conflicting instructions, stale context, false completion, and malformed tool results.\\n+7. **Economics:** cold start, throughput, memory, error rate, provider cost, and transfer cost.\\n+\\n+Store raw probe outputs remotely or in a cold tier, but keep the scored summary and output hashes local.\\n+\\n+## First dogfood loop\\n+\\n+1. Choose five currently used models and record exact provider/model identifiers.\\n+2. Run the same small probe pack through each model.\\n+3. Generate five RIB passports and lineage edges.\\n+4. Ask the router to select a model using only the passports and budget policy.\\n+5. Dispatch one real but reversible job to Vast.\\n+6. Compare predicted versus observed cost, latency, quality, and failure mode.\\n+7. Commit a receipt and update the passports.\\n+\\n+This tests whether the atlas improves routing before we buy local storage or GPU hardware.\\n+\\n+## Decision law\\n+\\n+> The RIB may tell us where the model is, how to run it, what it tends to do, and when to distrust it. It may not claim to contain the model itself.\\n+\\n+The compact library is valuable precisely because it turns a fleet of opaque artifacts into inspectable, queryable, reproducible structure while leaving expensive weights offloaded until demanded.\\n*** End Patch\";\ntext(await tools.apply_patch(patch));\n", "internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough": {"turn_id": "01a058d2-1ea5-7cd1-bd45-dbf9bd0579ca", "create_time": 1788196561.489551}}

C:\\\\Users\\\\foste\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-08-30\\\\wh\\\\outputs\\\\MODEL_RIB_LIBRARY_DESIGN_2026-08-31.md\\n@@\\n ## Thesis\\n@@\\n The library is a **model genome/atlas**, not a replacement for model weights. The RIB describes how to locate, instantiate, test, compare, and use a model; the weights remain remote territory until a job needs them.\\n+\\n+## Governing law: the deterministic\u2013stochastic boundary\\n+\\n+The RIB sits at the boundary between two kinds of reality:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+DETERMINISTIC MAP                         STOCHASTIC TERRITORY\\n+identity, hashes, lineage                 model weights and latent knowledge\\n+schemas, prompts, probes                  sampled outputs\\n+budgets, leases, routing                  provider/runtime variance\\n+Docker recipes, tool contracts            corpus/order/hardware effects\\n+receipts and confidence                   rare and adversarial behaviors\\n+              \\\\                         /\\n+               \\\\  measurement boundary /\\n+                \\\\                     /\\n+                 RIB experiment receipt\\n+```\\n+\\n+The deterministic layer must specify the experiment: exact model revision, input hashes, probe version, sampling settings, tool order, runtime image, budget, and timeout. The stochastic layer produces observations. The receipt converts those observations into durable evidence without collapsing uncertainty into a fake certainty.\\n+\\n+Therefore a model passport stores distributions, ranges, coverage, and confidence where appropriate\u2014not one permanent label such as \u201csmart,\u201d \u201csafe,\u201d or \u201cuncensored.\u201d Repeating the same probe under the same conditions is part of the evidence model; disagreement is data about variance, not automatically a bug.\\n+\\n+The build loop is:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+deterministic RIB experiment\\n+        -> stochastic model/provider encounter\\n+        -> deterministic receipt of outputs, hashes, metrics, and cost\\n+        -> graph update with confidence and coverage\\n+```\\n+\\n+This is why the atlas can remain compact while retaining nuance: it stores the stable structures and the measured boundaries of the unstable behavior.\\n*** End Patch\";\ntext(await tools.apply_patch(patch));\n", "internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough": {"turn_id": "01a058d2-f0a2-73c2-a308-dcf36e533157", "create_time": 1788196615.191985}}

C:\\\\Users\\\\foste\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-08-30\\\\wh\\\\outputs\\\\SHADOW_WORK_SALON_2026-08-31.md\\n+# Shadow Work Salon \u2014 Reading the Unmapped System\\n+\\n+**Date:** 2026-08-31  \\n+**Method:** Basecamp climb, elder ruling, staggered salon, Riddler taint, switchboard boundary, Dirac lifecycle, rightsizer economics  \\n+**Scope:** Mag/OpenClaw, boards, salons, MCP surfaces, model atlas, flywheel/offload, receipts, and the operator\u2019s conversation as evidence  \\n+**Status:** design and audit artifact; no claim of host deployment\\n+\\n+## The ruling\\n+\\n+In this system, \u201cshadow work\u201d means finding behavior that is real in the territory but absent, implicit, duplicated, unreceipted, or misclassified in the map.\\n+\\n+The shadow is not a supernatural organ. It is the gap between:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+what the system says exists\\n+what a caller can reach\\n+what actually executes\\n+what state changes\\n+what receipt proves the change\\n+what the next session can recover\\n+```\\n+\\n+The most important correction from this salon is that **repetition is not automatically noise**. Repetition is an observation channel. It can mean emphasis, unresolved disagreement, convergence, a hidden invariant, a provider failure, or a runaway retry loop. The system must classify it before suppressing it.\\n+\\n+The current failure mode is not \u201cwe repeat.\u201d It is \u201cwe repeat without extracting the signal, and we sometimes mistake repeated intention for completed state.\u201d\\n+\\n+## What the internal salon used\\n+\\n+The salon is a bounded set of views over the same evidence, not a chorus that grants authority.\\n+\\n+| Seat | Question | Deliverable |\\n+|---|---|---|\\n+| Basecamp / elder | What is claimed, what is measured, and what is still unknown? | status law and source-of-truth ruling |\\n+| Riddler | What information is hidden, tainted, or leaking across surfaces? | provenance and audience envelope |\\n+| Dirac | Which lifecycle edge repeats, disappears, or never closes? | transition graph and open-cycle list |\\n+| Switchboard / governor | Can speech, consensus, or a retry become authority? | typed proposal and effect boundary |\\n+| Mycelial queue | Is repetition feeding useful work or feeding itself? | lease, backpressure, and dedupe diagnosis |\\n+| Model atlas | Is the same phrase a model invariant, a prompt artifact, or a provider-specific quirk? | cross-lineage comparison |\\n+| Rightsizer / operator | What should happen now, later, cheaply, or never? | next action with budget and stop rule |\\n+\\n+Each seat produces an observation, a falsifier, and one bounded repair. A seat does not declare an organ live merely because it can describe one.\\n+\\n+## The shadow layers\\n+\\n+### 1. Shadow authority\\n+\\n+Direct CLI, MCP, board, desktop, or provider paths can bypass the switchboard/effect broker. A roast can look like a command; a consensus pack can look like authorization; a \u201csuccessful\u201d function call can look like a completed side effect.\\n+\\n+**Required invariant:** speech may create a typed proposal, never permission. Only the governor/reference monitor grants an effect, and only the effect broker commits the receipt.\\n+\\n+### 2. Shadow memory\\n+\\n+Conversation JSONL, backups, caches, stale indexes, provider traces, workshop artifacts, and board lines may contain the evidence needed to reconstruct a task but may not be in the shared map. A successor session then sees a summary without knowing what was omitted.\\n+\\n+**Required invariant:** every handoff has a content hash, line/file pointer, freshness, taint, and enough compact state to resume without loading the original transcript.\\n+\\n+### 3. Shadow computation\\n+\\n+Timeouts, retries, compaction attempts, duplicate requests, orphaned workers, and provider calls that continue after the caller gives up can consume resources without appearing as useful work.\\n+\\n+**Required invariant:** `submitted`, `running`, `timed_out`, `cancel_requested`, `cancelled`, `receipt_committed`, and `failed` are distinct states. A timeout is not proof that execution stopped.\\n+\\n+### 4. Shadow identity\\n+\\n+The same logical task may appear under a dashboard session, OpenClaw session, Mag task, provider request, board post, worker claim, and Verkle artifact without a stable join key. Host Hermes, Docker OpenClaw, Mag routing, and local/remote workers can therefore look like one organism while acting as several.\\n+\\n+**Required invariant:** `request_id`, `session_id`, `turn_id`, `task_id`, `provider`, `model`, and `artifact_digest` travel together across every surface.\\n+\\n+### 5. Shadow economics\\n+\\n+Token usage, subscription limits, quotas, free lanes, local GPU time, Vast jobs, latency, cache hits, and off-hours preference are not useful if they cannot be joined to the work that caused them.\\n+\\n+**Required invariant:** each route decision records expected cost, actual cost when known, quality/latency class, quota state, and why it ran now versus later.\\n+\\n+### 6. Shadow state\\n+\\n+`queued`, `claimed`, `authorized`, `working`, `complete`, and \u201cthe agent replied\u201d are frequently treated as interchangeable. They are not.\\n+\\n+**Required invariant:** only a durable artifact plus a valid receipt can move a task to `RECEIPT_COMMITTED` or `LIVE`.\\n+\\n+### 7. Shadow social governance\\n+\\n+Personas, roasts, salons, and model agreement are useful search mechanisms. They become dangerous when volume is treated as authority. A repeated claim can be important, wrong, injected, or merely copied.\\n+\\n+**Required invariant:** agreement, independence, evidence quality, and authority remain separate fields.\\n+\\n+### 8. Shadow territory\\n+\\n+Names such as atlas, basecamp, elder, fireball-cycle, effect broker, blackboard, and hypervisor have appeared at different times as doctrine, files, staged patches, live callers, or metaphors. The disagreement between previous audits\u2014some reporting ghosts, later evidence reporting partial live surfaces\u2014is itself a finding.\\n+\\n+**Required invariant:** every status claim is source-scoped and time-scoped. A generated map says `UNKNOWN` when it lacks a current receipt.\\n+\\n+### 9. Shadow ecology\\n+\\n+The system has positive feedback paths:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+context growth -> compaction pressure -> recovery text -> more context\\n+retry -> duplicate request -> queue pressure -> more retry\\n+board summon -> reply -> summon -> board volume\\n+agent uncertainty -> more agents -> less budget/context per agent\\n+```\\n+\\n+**Required invariant:** each loop has a bounded turn count, lease, expiry, backpressure signal, and stop condition.\\n+\\n+## Repetition is a sensor, not a defect\\n+\\n+The same text or idea can carry several different meanings. The map should preserve the raw occurrence and attach a classification rather than deleting it as \u201cduplicate.\u201d\\n+\\n+| Repetition class | What it may mean | Evidence to inspect | Safe action |\\n+|---|---|---|---|\\n+| `EMPHASIS` | Operator or seat keeps pointing at an important unresolved concern | recurrence across time/surfaces; no state closure | promote to an explicit question or invariant |\\n+| `CONVERGENCE` | Independent seats found the same answer | independent lineage, distinct prompts, shared evidence | increase confidence, not authority |\\n+| `NOVELTY_CLUSTER` | A repeated phrase surrounds a new detail or unexplained edge | delta tokens/entities/relations per occurrence | extract the delta and run one probe |\\n+| `CONTRADICTION` | Same subject recurs with changed claims | polarity, version, source, timestamp | open a falsifier task; do not average away |\\n+| `MODEL_INVARIANT` | Multiple models behave similarly under controlled probes | same prompt envelope, different providers/lineages | add to atlas with confidence and probe recipe |\\n+| `PROVIDER_FAILURE` | Same error repeats from one lane | provider, credential, endpoint, timeout, request IDs | quarantine or reroute; retain cost evidence |\\n+| `RETRY_LOOP` | Same operation repeats without state delta | same task/effect, short interval, no receipt | stop/reap/backoff and emit loop receipt |\\n+| `CONTEXT_DUPLICATION` | Repeated transcript or tool output is consuming the window | hashes, token estimates, pack lineage | replace bytes with pointer plus digest |\\n+| `SOCIAL_AMPLIFICATION` | Copies increase but independent evidence does not | lineage and copy graph | collapse display, preserve raw provenance |\\n+| `ORPHAN_ECHO` | A task keeps being mentioned after its owner or receipt vanished | task/owner/receipt join | reopen as unknown, not complete |\\n+\\n+### The three scores\\n+\\n+These are analysis scores, not permissions:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+emphasis_score = recurrence\\n+               * cross_surface_spread\\n+               * temporal_persistence\\n+               * unresolvedness\\n+\\n+loop_score = recurrence\\n+           * same_effect_similarity\\n+           * failure_similarity\\n+           * inverse_state_delta\\n+           * short_time_window\\n+\\n+novelty_score = new_entities + new_relations + changed_claims\\n+              + new_falsifiers + new_receipt_edges\\n+```\\n+\\n+Normalize each score and retain the factors. A high emphasis score says \u201cinvestigate.\u201d A high loop score says \u201cshed or stop.\u201d A high novelty score says \u201cextract a new probe.\u201d None says \u201cexecute.\u201d\\n+\\n+### What this changes in the flywheel\\n+\\n+The flywheel becomes:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+observe -> cluster repeated signals -> classify repetition\\n+       -> extract delta or detect loop -> choose bounded probe\\n+       -> route cheaply or immediately -> commit artifact/receipt\\n+       -> update map and repetition ledger -> repeat only if unresolved\\n+```\\n+\\n+The system no longer has to choose between retaining everything and deleting duplicates. It retains lossless evidence, serves a compact semantic view, and exposes only the relevant delta to the next seat.\\n+\\n+## Salon positions\\n+\\n+### Basecamp / elder\\n+\\n+**Observation:** the current map is strong at declarations and imports, uneven at wiring, and weakest at live transitions and recovery. A verified manifest does not prove a working context handoff or offload completion.\\n+\\n+**Challenge:** do not create a \u201cshadow organ\u201d just because shadow behavior was named. The first deliverable is a generated report from existing evidence.\\n+\\n+**Falsifier:** if the generated report cannot distinguish a staged file, a callable surface, a caller, and a receipt-backed transition, the map compiler is not done.\\n+\\n+**Repair:** make `DECLARED`, `INSTRUMENTED`, `WIRED`, `STATEFUL`, `VERIFIED`, `LIVE`, and `GHOST` source- and time-scoped.\\n+\\n+### Riddler\\n+\\n+**Observation:** the same evidence needs different information envelopes. Public-safe redaction can remove cost and provenance that the internal rightsizer needs.\\n+\\n+**Challenge:** \u201cshared\u201d must not mean \u201cunclassified.\u201d\\n+\\n+**Falsifier:** a shared pack contains a secret, or an internal pack cannot explain where its claim came from.\\n+\\n+**Repair:** use `internal_lossless`, `shared_semantic`, and `public_safe` modes. Every repeated item carries `taint`, `source_digest`, `line_span`, `freshness`, and `confidence`.\\n+\\n+### Dirac\\n+\\n+**Observation:** the interesting object is the transition graph, not the list of organs. Repetition often identifies an edge that never closes.\\n+\\n+**Challenge:** a loop in the board is not necessarily a loop in execution; a loop in execution may never be visible on the board.\\n+\\n+**Falsifier:** operational lifecycle edges are absent while the scan reports a clean graph.\\n+\\n+**Repair:** feed Dirac the real graph:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+append -> pressure -> checkpoint -> shed/repack -> route\\n+      -> execute/offload -> artifact -> receipt -> archive\\n+      -> map_refresh -> successor_resume\\n+```\\n+\\n+### Switchboard / governor\\n+\\n+**Observation:** repeated imperatives and consensus are inputs to classification, not grants.\\n+\\n+**Challenge:** a clever model may rephrase an effect until a permissive path accepts it.\\n+\\n+**Falsifier:** any free-text board line can directly invoke a side effect, or a proposal can grant more capability than requested.\\n+\\n+**Repair:** closed-enum effect types, explicit capability sets, TTL/budget, target consent where relevant, and a single effect broker. Refuse stale or unreceipted transitions.\\n+\\n+### Mycelial queue\\n+\\n+**Observation:** recurrence can be a useful demand signal or an organism feeding itself. `queued` is not `offloaded`; a summon is not a lease.\\n+\\n+**Challenge:** without expiry and backpressure, the salon rewards prolific models and starves quiet useful workers.\\n+\\n+**Falsifier:** a job can be claimed twice, retried indefinitely, or marked complete without a durable artifact.\\n+\\n+**Repair:** one owner, one lease, explicit expiry, dedupe key, bounded retry, and a batch receipt for backlog reconciliation.\\n+\\n+### Model atlas / game-world explorer\\n+\\n+**Observation:** repeated behavior across models is a possible invariant, but only controlled probes can separate model law from prompt contamination, provider wrapper, or copied context.\\n+\\n+**Challenge:** \u201call models agree\u201d may mean all models saw the same untrusted answer.\\n+\\n+**Falsifier:** the behavior disappears when prompt order, temperature, system envelope, or provider changes.\\n+\\n+**Repair:** store probe envelope, model revision, provider, decoding knobs, raw result digest, extracted invariant, counterexample, and confidence. Agreement raises confidence; it never authorizes an effect.\\n+\\n+### Rightsizer / operator\\n+\\n+**Observation:** repetition is a scheduling signal. Persistent emphasis may deserve immediate attention; a provider retry loop should be shed; a novel delta can go to a cheap extractor.\\n+\\n+**Challenge:** the cheapest route is not always the smallest token bill if it creates more retries or loses recoverability.\\n+\\n+**Falsifier:** route selection cannot explain why work ran now, later, locally, or remotely.\\n+\\n+**Repair:** attach budget, urgency, quality class, latency ceiling, quota, cache value, and off-hours eligibility to the route receipt.\\n+\\n+## The minimum dogfood experiment\\n+\\n+Do this on existing conversation and board evidence before adding another named organ.\\n+\\n+### Input\\n+\\n+Use a bounded slice of:\\n+\\n+- this conversation\u2019s repeated claims about context shedding, switchboard, blackboard, atlas, MCP, model library, and offload;\\n+- the current board pack and its `.` summon responses;\\n+- the Basecamp organ audit;\\n+- the model atlas/library design docs;\\n+- current trajectory and usage receipts where IDs exist.\\n+\\n+### Procedure\\n+\\n+1. Normalize each occurrence without deleting the raw text.\\n+2. Attach source, timestamp, surface, speaker/seat, model/provider if known, and hash.\\n+3. Cluster by semantic subject, not exact string alone.\\n+4. Label each cluster with one primary repetition class and optional secondary classes.\\n+5. Compute recurrence, independence, temporal spread, novelty delta, state delta, and receipt coverage.\\n+6. Select the highest-value unresolved cluster.\\n+7. Run exactly one bounded probe or one bounded repair.\\n+8. Write a receipt even if the probe fails or produces no novelty.\\n+9. Update the map; do not promote a new organ from a single repeated claim.\\n+\\n+### Required receipt shape\\n+\\n+```json\\n+{\\n+  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"shadow_repetition_receipt.v1\\\",\\n+  \\\"cluster_id\\\": \\\"content-addressed-id\\\",\\n+  \\\"subject\\\": \\\"context_admission\\\",\\n+  \\\"class\\\": [\\\"EMPHASIS\\\", \\\"NOVELTY_CLUSTER\\\"],\\n+  \\\"occurrences\\\": 0,\\n+  \\\"surfaces\\\": [],\\n+  \\\"lineages\\\": [],\\n+  \\\"source_digests\\\": [],\\n+  \\\"novelty_delta\\\": [],\\n+  \\\"state_delta_before\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"state_delta_after\\\": null,\\n+  \\\"falsifier\\\": \\\"\\\",\\n+  \\\"probe_or_repair\\\": \\\"\\\",\\n+  \\\"result\\\": \\\"receipt_committed|failed|expired|unknown\\\",\\n+  \\\"artifact_digest\\\": \\\"\\\",\\n+  \\\"taint\\\": \\\"untrusted_evidence\\\",\\n+  \\\"freshness\\\": \\\"\\\",\\n+  \\\"cost\\\": {\\\"input\\\": null, \\\"output\\\": null, \\\"actual\\\": null},\\n+  \\\"next_action\\\": Water, bubbles, mycelium, and flock animation are not interchangeable computers; they are candidate reservoirs whose useful behavior must be measured.\\n+\\n+**Guardrail:** \u201cworks as a metaphor\u201d is not \u201cworks as a computation.\u201d The minimum proof is a repeatable input/output task, a calibration record, and a receipt.\\n+\\n+### Lens B \u2014 game genome and cache\\n+\\n+**Sources:** `game.txt`, `game2.txt`, `game3.txt`, `new 21.txt`, `watch/corpus/`, `BASECAMP_GAME_ATLAS_20260901.md`, and the game research/salon files.\\n+\\n+**Question:** Which rules are invariant, which parameters vary, and which state must never be cached as if it were a rule?\\n+\\n+**Steal:** use the six-function contract\u2014state encoding, initial state, legality, transition, terminal, scoring\u2014as the universal L0. The full transcript is the archive; the RIB is a compact, attributed intermediate representation containing anchors, tool/result pairs, paths, hashes, acceptance commands, and unresolved disputes. The deterministic engine owns legal transitions; the narrator renders them; the Verkle/RIB trail preserves what actually happened.\\n+\\n+**Guardrail:** atmosphere may propose a move, but only the engine can make it legal.\\n+\\n+## 3. Self-steal findings\\n+\\n+### What repeats and therefore matters\\n+\\n+1. **Stable core / dynamic tail** repeats across caching, games, RIBs, bubbles, and model lanes. This is the strongest cross-domain invariant.\\n+2. **Boundary conditions** repeat across authority, physics, prompt scopes, and game legality. Most failures are boundary failures, not generative failures.\\n+3. **The verifier must be outside the narrator.** Engines, receipts, hash checks, and health probes are the anti-confabulation layer.\\n+4. **Local canonical, remote replaceable** repeats across Verkle handoff, model custody, MCP, and the shared inbox.\\n+5. **Failure is data only when classified.** A timeout, stale receipt, duplicate source, model overload, and false completion need different labels.\\n+6. **The operator is the non-transferable root.** Models can propose, rank, criticize, and execute bounded effects; C:\\\\Users\\\\foste\\\\Documents\\\\projects\\\\local_sovereign_agent\\\\docs\\\\ref\\\\VERKLE_KZG_BOUNDARY_20260901.md\\n+# Verkle/KZG Boundary \u2014 What We Have, What It Means\\n+\\n+Status: shared explanatory note \u00b7 2026-09-01\\n+\\n+## The clean distinction\\n+\\n+Mag's live `verkle_knot` organ is a content-addressed, append-only SHA-256\\n+Merkle ledger. It has leaves, prefix roots, sibling-path membership proofs, a\\n+tip, a lock, and repair tooling. It is useful and currently passing its chain\\n+and proof gates.\\n+\\n+It is **not** yet a KZG Verkle tree. The name describes the intended role and\\n+upgrade path; it does not prove that polynomial commitments exist in the\\n+runtime.\\n+\\n+The executable facts are in `mag/verkle_knot.py`: leaf hashing uses\\n+`SHA256(\\\"leaf:\\\" || canonical_json)`, internal hashing uses\\n+`SHA256(\\\"node:\\\" || left || \\\":\\\" || right)`, and an odd node is duplicated. The\\n+proof is an index plus sibling hashes. There is no finite-field polynomial,\\n+elliptic-curve point, SRS, or pairing check in that path.\\n+\\n+## KZG in one page\\n+\\n+KZG (Kate\u2013Zaverucha\u2013Goldberg) commits to a polynomial without publishing all\\n+of its coefficients.\\n+\\n+Given a polynomial\\n+\\n+```text\\n+p(X) = c0 + c1 X + ... + cd X^d\\n+```\\n+\\n+the setup publishes curve points `[\u03c4^0]G1, [\u03c4^1]G1, ...` for a hidden setup\\n+value `\u03c4`. The commitment is:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+C = [p(\u03c4)]G1 = c0[\u03c4^0]G1 + c1[\u03c4^1]G1 + ... + cd[\u03c4^d]G1\\n+```\\n+\\n+To prove that `p(z) = y`, the prover forms:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+q(X) = (p(X) - y) / (X - z)\\n+\u03c0 = [q(\u03c4)]G1\\n+```\\n+\\n+The verifier checks one pairing relation:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+e(C - [y]G1, G2) = e(\u03c0, [\u03c4]G2 - [z]G2)\\n+```\\n+\\n+The point is not that the verifier knows the whole polynomial. It knows a\\n+small commitment and checks a local opening against that commitment. That is\\n+why KZG can make a wide Verkle node practical: 256 child slots are encoded as\\n+values of one degree-255 polynomial, and a path proves one selected slot per\\n+level.\\n+\\n+## Mapping to our system\\n+\\n+| Our organ | Current meaning | Genuine KZG/Verkle counterpart |\\n+|---|---|---|\\n+| `verkle_chain.jsonl` | ordered session-leaf history | canonical state/version history |\\n+| `verkle_tip.json` | current SHA-256 root pointer | published root commitment |\\n+| `*.knot.json` | leaf payload and its SHA-256 fingerprint | immutable leaf bytes / field value |\\n+| sibling path | binary Merkle membership proof | 32 wide-node KZG openings plus child-link hashes |\\n+| `topic_evolution.json` | derived view | derived index, never root authority |\\n+| Q-state / RIB / game stores | separate memory lineages | separate namespaces bridged by explicit hashes |\\n+| `by-session_*.json` | convenience pointer, currently truncated | must become collision-free content index |\\n+\\n+## What defragmentation means here\\n+\\n+Defragmentation is not flattening every memory into one giant chain. It is\\n+making the seams explicit:\\n+\\n+1. Freeze the current root as `legacy_sha256_merkle.v1`.\\n+2. Preserve source bytes and backups; build a derived index containing path,\\n+   schema, content hash, lineage, chain index, and root membership.\\n+3. Replace truncated session pointers with full-session or hash-addressed keys.\\n+4. Keep Q-state, RIB/trajectory, game/world, and biography as distinct\\n+   lineages with bridge receipts.\\n+5. Add `verkle_kzg.v1` beside the legacy root, with canonical bytes, pinned\\n+   BLS12-381 parameters, a public SRS digest, cross-implementation fixtures,\\n+   and neutral verification.\\n+6.
